Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0015", "row_sha256": "51828d895feafdd0fc773284ee67601974a9082391ab11d0190dccedc92bab7b", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
can you turn these notes into one ordinary public update about next week's schedule at North Window Radio, the independent community station in Bellwether. it's for listeners, not an internal memo, and it should read like a real station notice, not a promotion. use the week of monday october 13 through sunday october 19, 2025 as the time frame. explain the schedule changes clearly, but don't make it sound like the entire grid has been rebuilt. people have asked what's moving and whether the programs themselves are changing, so keep those things distinct. this is one fictional episode/update, not a general description of how radio schedules work.

some context that should be in there without taking over the piece: North Window Radio is member-supported and its studio is in the old library annex on Alder Street. listeners can still find the paper schedule on the board by the annex entrance, and the station's online grid is updated by Mina Calder, the schedule editor. the point of the notice is the coming week's practical changes. no need to invent a phone number, a website, funding figures, or an explanation of the station's entire history. mention that the programs are staying the same where that's what the notes say; don't imply hosts or show formats are changing just because a time changes.

here are the actual grid details, sorry if they're in a weird order. the weekday program Morning Window stays monday through friday from 6:00 to 8:00 a.m. no change to those hours. Market Table, also weekdays, currently starts at 8:00 and is half an hour; from monday october 13 it starts at 8:30 and ends at 9:00 a.m. its host and content are unchanged. people who rely on that slot should be able to see the new time without hunting for it in a paragraph. Tuesday and Thursday Field Notes is currently 3:00 to 4:00 p.m.; starting tuesday october 14 it moves to 3:30 to 4:30 p.m. both weekly broadcasts move, it's not a one-time shift. the show itself is not getting a new name. Friday Night Cartography remains 8:00 to 9:00 p.m. and Saturday Open Desk remains 10:00 a.m. to noon, so mention them only if useful to show the rest of the week is steady. Sunday Shelf on sunday october 19 will be prerecorded rather than live, but it stays in its usual 6:00 to 7:00 p.m. hour. that's just for that date, not a permanent change. please don't accidentally make a list of all programs at the station if it distracts from these points.

there's a practical reason to explain briefly: work on a worn patch lead and some studio checks are under way, and the revised weekday timing leaves a little more room for the handoff between programs. don't claim the repair is finished or that it caused a broadcast failure. the schedule change is what listeners need first. keep the language plain and not alarmist. A numbered section would make sense for the two recurring time changes, maybe one heading and a short numbered list, but the whole thing should still feel like a connected update with paragraphs rather than a bare table. one ordinary quote from Rob Imani, the station engineer, can help. quote exactly: “we can keep the studio schedule moving, but the ridge side is still a separate check.” don't turn that into a claim that transmission has been cleared or that the station has a problem on air.

there's also the engineer's last assessment, and i need the limits kept with it, not boiled down into something broader. Rob's bench check on october 8 tested the studio console clock, the studio monitor feed, and the local recording logger. each ran continuously for 45 minutes on studio power, and he observed no dropouts during that test interval. The test did not include the ridge transmitter, the antenna, the remote link, or the emergency generator. The temporary 12-meter patch lead between the studio rack and the encoder has to stay fully seated; if its connector loosens, the logger may stop capturing the program feed. if that happens, the duty host is to note the start and end time and switch to the spare recorder. say that the assessment covers studio-side playback and logging under the test setup only. it does not establish off-air reception, transmission coverage, or backup-power performance. A separate visit to the ridge is booked for october 16, weather permitting; no result from that visit is available yet. keep the if-condition and the limited scope close to the assessment, rather than making it sound like an overall pass or failure. this is important but it shouldn't swallow the schedule notice or get repeated later as a summary.

finally, there is a different bit of station information that belongs at the end as its own paragraph, not as a conclusion about the equipment. North Window Radio will have a public open studio on sunday november 2, from 2:00 to 4:00 p.m. at the old library annex on Alder Street. visitors should sign in at the front desk; no advance RSVP is needed. keep that separate from the october schedule dates so nobody mistakes the open studio for part of next week's grid. make the finished notice self-contained and readable for a listener who hasn't seen these notes. include the exact dates, days, times, names, and conditions above, use a natural short heading if helpful, and don't add an outcome or recommendation beyond what's here. the final paragraph should carry the open-studio information as distinct news, not an invented wrap-up.", "output": "Write one self-contained, listener-facing public update about the coming week’s schedule at North Window Radio, the independent, member-supported community station in Bellwether. The update should cover Monday, October 13 through Sunday, October 19, 2025. Use plain, ordinary language and a natural short heading if helpful. Make it read like a station notice, not an internal memo or promotion. Explain the practical schedule changes without suggesting that the whole grid has been rebuilt, and distinguish changes in broadcast time from changes to a program or its host. Do not invent a phone number, website, funding figures, station history, or other details.

North Window Radio’s studio is in the old library annex on Alder Street. The paper schedule is posted on the board by the annex entrance, and schedule editor Mina Calder updates the online grid. Mention these details only as useful context for listeners.

Present the following schedule information clearly, using a short numbered section if it suits the update:

1. Morning Window remains Monday through Friday, 6:00–8:00 a.m. Market Table, also on weekdays, moves from 8:00–8:30 a.m. to 8:30–9:00 a.m., beginning Monday, October 13. Its host and content are unchanged.
2. Field Notes airs Tuesdays and Thursdays. Beginning Tuesday, October 14, both weekly broadcasts move from 3:00–4:00 p.m. to 3:30–4:30 p.m. The program name does not change.

Friday Night Cartography remains Fridays, 8:00–9:00 p.m., and Saturday Open Desk remains Saturdays, 10:00 a.m.–noon. Sunday Shelf airs Sunday, October 19, in its usual 6:00–7:00 p.m. hour, but will be prerecorded rather than live on that date only. Do not present that as a permanent change or let other program details distract from the listed changes.

Briefly explain that work on a worn patch lead and studio checks are under way, and that the revised weekday timing leaves a little more room for the handoff between programs. Do not say that the repair is finished or caused a broadcast failure. Keep the schedule information prominent and the tone calm. Include this exact quote from station engineer Rob Imani: “we can keep the studio schedule moving, but the ridge side is still a separate check.” Do not interpret it as confirmation that transmission has been cleared or as a claim that the station has an on-air problem.

Include Rob’s October 8 bench-check assessment with its limits and conditions intact. The studio console clock, studio monitor feed, and local recording logger each ran continuously for 45 minutes on studio power, with no dropouts observed during that test interval. The test did not include the ridge transmitter, antenna, remote link, or emergency generator. The temporary 12-meter patch lead between the studio rack and encoder must remain fully seated; if its connector loosens, the logger may stop capturing the program feed. If that happens, the duty host is to note the start and end time and switch to the spare recorder. State that the assessment covers studio-side playback and logging under the test setup only; it does not establish off-air reception, transmission coverage, or backup-power performance. A separate ridge visit is booked for October 16, weather permitting, and no result is available yet. Keep the conditional instruction and limited scope close to the assessment. Do not describe the assessment as an overall pass or failure, and do not repeat it later as a summary.

End with a separate final paragraph containing this distinct station information: North Window Radio will hold a public open studio on Sunday, November 2, from 2:00–4:00 p.m. at the old library annex on Alder Street. Visitors should sign in at the front desk; no advance RSVP is needed. Keep this separate from the October schedule dates so readers do not mistake it for part of the coming week’s grid. Make no additions, outcomes, or recommendations beyond the supplied information."}]
